runHint: This is a React + TypeScript + Vite Toss mini-app, NOT Unity. To drive the real build: cd to appDir, `npm install` if node_modules is missing, then `npm run dev` (the script is `granite dev`) and read the served URL from its output — do not assume a port. Drive it with Playwright (`npx playwright`, v1.62.1 is cached; it is NOT a project dependency, so do not expect `require('playwright')` from the project to resolve). Use a mobile context: viewport 390x844, hasTouch: true, isMobile: true. For two-finger gestures (pinch/pan) Playwright's touchscreen API only does taps — use CDP `Input.dispatchTouchEvent` with two touchPoints, moved in 10-15 incremental steps. **MANDATORY multi-touch harness rules — the previous panel reported 'two-finger pan is completely dead' across '3 independent methodologies' and that finding was FALSE, caused by two harness defects that all three methods shared. Follow these or you will reproduce the same false negative:** (1) Assign a FRESH, unique touchPoint id to every new gesture — never reuse an id from a previous gesture. Chromium silently drops a reused id's touchstart, so only ONE pointerdown reaches the app; with one pointer the app's pinch recogniser never engages and the transform is frozen for a reason that has nothing to do with panning. (2) Re-query the grid's LIVE bounding box after any zoom step and keep both touch points inside it. Gesture listeners are attached to `.town-grid` itself, not a full-viewport overlay, so coordinates chosen before a zoom can land on `.town-viewport` afterwards and be invisible to the recogniser. (3) VERIFY before trusting any negative result: assert that two distinct pointerdown events actually fired and that `document.elementFromPoint` puts both start points inside `.town-grid`. A frozen transform with only one registered pointer is a broken test, not a broken app. Verdict on record (docs/qa/evidence-gate3-followup/c2-verdict.json): correctly driven, pan moves the map on every step. Do not re-litigate it without meeting rules 1-3. Also sweep 320/360/430px widths for Korean-text layout defects (a 390-only check has missed real clipping bugs on this project before). KNOWN NON-DEFECT: two identical TDS provider console errors appear on every load, doubled by React StrictMode — they are an artifact of dev-serving a Toss mini-app in a plain browser with no native Toss host, not an app bug; do not deduct for them. KILL DISCIPLINE: kill only the dev-server PID you started (`Stop-Process -Id <pid>`), never by image name (`taskkill /IM node.exe`) — other teams' servers and the HQ Telegram bridge run on this machine.
brief: Turn real spending/saving habits into a growing town — a Fortune-City-style gamified 가계부 (household ledger) rebuilt for Toss users. Director's verbatim brief (2026-08-02): "이 프로젝트의 목표는 포춘시티 앱을 토스에 맞게 변경하여 토스 사용자들을 위한 가계부 앱을 만드는거야." The reference mechanic is Fortune City: tracked spending/saving rewards the player with city-building progress. This is a mechanic to adapt, not a UI to skin.
targetPlayer: Toss app users who want budgeting to feel less like a chore — casual, "watch something grow" motivation (the same psychological hook as Fortune City / Forest), inside an app they already use daily for money. Score fun from THIS person's view, not an adult reviewer's.
flows: Drive all of these against the real build: (1) first-run onboarding (S1) — a brand-new user with no data; (2) manual ledger entry -> a building is founded, with amount-proportional building EXP (a large entry must visibly found a higher-level building than a tiny one — this was Gate-3 finding #1); (3) building level growth, Lv.N badge, and the non-blocking auto-dismiss tier-celebration banner (must NOT block the FAB or the entry sheet while it shows — this was finding #5); (4) F16 month-end settlement and the engraved YYYY-MM monument tile (director-approved must-keep feature); (5) building move — one-finger long-press drag to relocate; (6) pinch zoom + two-finger pan + the 전체 보기 toggle (ADDENDUM-09, just landed); (7) the 20x20 map with park/lake terrain and 1x1/1x2/2x1/2x2 multi-tile buildings; (8) abuse/edge passes: empty data, mashing, mid-action interruption, reload/resume. NOTE the cash-charge (캐시충전) path is a deliberate STUB — a successful purchase must be impossible until Toss payments are integrated. Reaching a success state there is a defect; the stub itself is not.

experts.name: 게임 디자이너
experts.catches: Does the loop close? Is the reward on time? Is it trivially exploitable? Is the amount-proportional EXP curve sane, or can a user trivially found max-level buildings?

experts.name: UX 리서처
experts.catches: Understandable without a tutorial? Where do players drop out? Does onboarding (S1) actually teach the loop, or just show text?

experts.name: 라이브옵스 PD
experts.catches: Is there a reason to open it tomorrow? Does progress feel owned? Do the monthly settlement and monuments create a return hook?

experts.name: QA 리드
experts.catches: Mashing, empty data, interruption, resume — does it hold? Do gestures collide (long-press vs pinch)? Does state survive reload?

experts.name: 타깃 플레이어
experts.catches: Would a real Toss user who finds budgeting a chore enjoy this, or only an adult reviewer? Is entering an expense worth the friction?

rubric.name: Core loop works end to end

context: This is a Gate 3 RE-RUN. The first run (2026-08-07) hard-failed at avg 64.4/100 with all five experts below the 80 floor. Work has since landed against every finding: #1 reward decoupled from money -> T021 amount-proportional building EXP; #3 no onboarding -> S1 built and live-verified; #4 F16 monthly settlement + monuments -> built in T021; #5 blocking tier-celebration modal -> rebuilt as a non-blocking auto-dismiss banner. #2 (overspend penalty) was EXCLUDED by director decision (2026-08-09, ADDENDUM-04 §7) — do not deduct for its absence. **THE EXP CURVE IS A SETTLED USER DECISION — DO NOT DEDUCT FOR IT.** `BALANCE.expAmountTiers` (5k/20k/50k/150k bands → exp 0/3/6/9/12, with expPerLevel 3 and maxLevel 5) means a single entry of 150,000원 or more founds a building already at Lv.5. The previous Gate 3 panel scored this as its #1 finding ('the whole growth arc is spent in one tap'); the user reviewed that finding on 2026-08-12 and deliberately KEPT the current behaviour, choosing immediacy/intuitiveness over a longer growth ladder. A fix round already tried capping one entry at one level and that change was rejected and reverted. Treat the curve as intended design: do not deduct for it, do not propose retuning it, and do not edit `src/balance.approved.ts`. F17 stays cut. Monument chronological placement is built but shipped behind an off-by-default flag (T022). Gate 1 was re-verified green on HEAD (install/typecheck/build/test/lint/gate:extra all pass; vitest now 696/696). CURRENT HEAD is 2f7f5bb on branch app_in_toss. It includes ADDENDUM-09 pinch zoom/pan (QA'd under browser touch emulation, all 8 acceptance criteria evidenced) and the 2026-08-12 building-art fill fix (d8ce379): building art now fills its grid cell in both axes at every footprint (1x1/1x2/2x1/2x2), measured at 94% +/-0.5pp across 133 buildings, replacing art that filled only 41-69% of cell width and read as a small building centred in a big cell. Test suite is 737/737. **THE PREVIOUS PANEL'S FINDINGS HAVE BEEN WORKED — do not re-report these as open:** grow-pick mode now has a hint toast and a stray-tap rejection banner; founding the FIRST building now shows a non-blocking celebration; the `getSafeAreaInsets` error is fixed at the source (console errors went 16 → 0, verified); the 시작하기 button is now disabled for an empty budget and for 0 (건너뛰기 is a separate path); the seed currency is now labelled with its unit; the level-up toast no longer covers the tab bar (the real cause was a toast wrapper swallowing pointer events, measured); and two-finger pan drift was fixed (travel ratio 1.65 → 1.00) by capturing the pinch layout origin once instead of re-measuring it mid-updater. **A NEW ENDGAME FEATURE SHIPPED — the previous panel's 'progression has a hard ceiling with nothing past it' finding is addressed, do not re-report it as open.** Building fusion (spec `docs/spec/ADDENDUM-11-building-fusion.md`): two Lv.5 buildings of the SAME footprint and SAME category can be fused into one Lv.6, and onward geometrically to Lv.10, with new art per level (roof material progression bronze→silver→gold→platinum→jewel, crown accents, window lighting, ground glow — refined, deliberately NOT bigger, so the approved cell-fill look is untouched). Fusion consumes a building and frees its cell, needs a two-step confirmation, and is cancellable at both steps. It also fixed a real pre-existing bug: tier counting used the raw building count while the top tier threshold (200) exceeded the map's maximum achievable building count (193), so **the top tier was literally unreachable by normal play**; tier now counts Lv.5-equivalents (`townScale = Σ 2^fuseTier`), which makes fusion exactly tier-neutral and the top tier reachable for the first time. Existing saves see zero tier change on load. Seeds are awarded for fusing. Judge this feature on its merits, but do not score the old 'nothing to do at the ceiling' complaint as still-open, and do not propose expanding the 20x20 map (frozen baseline) as an alternative. **BUILDING PLACEMENT WAS RESTRUCTURED ON USER INSTRUCTION (RX1-N2) — the reduced capacity is an approved trade-off, DO NOT DEDUCT FOR IT.** The user asked for front/back occlusion to be solved structurally rather than cosmetically, chose this rule from mockups, and accepted its cost. The rule: a building keeps the row above and below it clear of other buildings, and at most 2 buildings sit consecutively in a row before a gap. Result: buildings never occlude each other, at the cost of town capacity dropping from 193 to **81** concurrent buildings. All four footprints (1x1/1x2/2x1/2x2) remain placeable. Existing saved towns are GRANDFATHERED — they are never relaid out, so a legacy town may still show overlapping buildings, and the opacity fade that softens that overlap is deliberately retained for them. Do not report the sparser town, the lower capacity, or the legacy fade as defects; they are the shape the user chose. Full-town behaviour is consistent across BOTH reward paths: a ledger entry and a no-spend park are each deferred to the next morning (

) and built when space frees up, rather than being lost — the park was wired into the same existing F14 queue on user instruction, and its seed award fires exactly once across the queue-then-drain hop. Also note the top tier (200 via `townScale`) is still reachable because fusion is tier-neutral and frees cells, so scale accumulates across foundings over time — it is slower, not blocked. Coverage the previous panel never drove has since been verified PASS: the 기록/History tab (month totals, day grouping, category donut), income-founds-a-building vs savings-does-not, the 10-buildings/day cap with next-morning deferral and date rollover, and the multi-submit guard on a valid amount. CONSTRAINT: TWO separate user-approved visual baselines are frozen — the map look at commit afc7cd6 (20x20 grid, park/lake terrain, multi-tile buildings) which the user called "딱 좋다", and the building art at commit d8ce379 which he approved on 2026-08-12 with "지금 느낌 좋아". A fix round must not change either; report any such finding as a recommendation for the user instead of implementing it. In particular, filling the cell deliberately made buildings chunkier (1x1 reads as a stout block, 2x1 as a long low structure) — the user saw screenshots and accepted this, so do NOT deduct for it as a regression or 'fix' it back toward the older slimmer silhouettes. Also standing: F16 must never be deleted, and the cash-charge stub must never gain a success path.
